title: Nature's Solution
subtitle: Like all good stories, this one has a wise druid too.

items.text: Nature's Solution
Bedroom, Suitcase
The night is quiet.
A melodic knock raps on the door, careful and a little hesitant.
With a soft click, the door opens on its own, spilling out a warm yellow glow.
She peeks her face in, almost like a dolphin bobbing her head out of the water.
A figure is waiting under the lamplight, just like the stories said.
Calm as a tree.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Hello.
Green eyes look into hers, patient, ready to listen.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Pardon me, I know it's late ... I worried you might already be resting.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: No need to be so formal, Miss Musician.
Nightfall is the only time she could squeeze in to come visit the reclusive lady.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I have a question. And it's really quite important to me, so ...

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: If it concerns me, I'm happy to offer what help I can. Please, ask.
Barcarola twists her fingers into her skirt. The hem bunches in her hands. The druid before her holds a quiet authority.
She hopes for—but also fears—the answer.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Ms. Druvis, I wanted to know ...

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: If there is a way to transplant Compassare.
Even a short rest between beats makes her heart clench.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: You mean you want to grow Compassare inside the suitcase?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Y-yes! Is that possible?

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Even in my time, it was rare. It only grows on remote islands far away.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: For a short time, plants like those became madly popular. Then, not long after really, they were replaced by pills and miracle elixirs.
The lady walks alongside creeping vines and silent trunks as she combs her memory.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: I suppose it was a matter of patience. There aren't many willing to wait around for a plant to grow.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: That's part of why, even when trade reached those islands, Compassare never made its way beyond them.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: I'm afraid that plants, like people, have homelands. Compassare cannot thrive anywhere else.
The answer strikes Barcarola with all the force of a broken string in the middle of a performance and carries with it the very same hot panic.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: You mean there's no way at all? I don't know much about plants, but what if I'm very careful? Like, incredibly, super careful?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Even if I might only grow one ...

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Plants are much pickier than you might imagine.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Perhaps you might plant it here, yes, but whatever grows from those seeds would no longer be Compassare.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: You mean it'd just be normal grass?

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: The people of Nukutaeao know their soil. They grow their Compassare in ways passed down through generations. It's more than just grass. It's an integral part of their culture.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: And culture cannot be so easily transplanted.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: But what about Fatutu?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: She used the last Compassare to make those Sea Mother's Eyes. It's my fault.
A quiet sigh.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: You came here for your friend.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I wanted to help her, but everything seemed more simple in my head.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Your friend already came to see me earlier.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: She knew the nature of Compassare. She knew what would happen when it left the island.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Still, she asked me whether there was any magic that could keep Compassare alive outside its home?
It was a simple, beautiful wish—one heartbreaking to answer.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: She thought I might be like a druid from a story she read, someone who could do anything. She placed her hopes in me.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: If we were truly inside a story, I would rewrite this chapter for her.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: But the story of nature can only be written by nature itself.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Thank you, Ms. Druvis.
A vine curls up to her shoulder, its open leaves brushing her cheek.
A small tree planted nearby, stirred awake by arcane skill, gently offers its presence.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: This is a Lumin tree. Its leaves and buds can glow. Break off a twig and place it in water. It will grow roots.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Once the roots clump, plant them in soil, and the branch will grow back into a tree.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Perhaps it will help you light up the night.
The water in the vase gently ripples as the Lumin branch sways.
Following guidance from her nature-loving friend, she trims the branch at a slanted angle, finds a slender-necked vase tucked away in the corner, and fills it with clear water.
Sure enough, it begins to glow, lighting up a small corner of the room.
The event is drawing near. She intends to bring this glowing branch with her today, hoping it will soothe the ripples in Fatutu's heart.
Bedroom, Suitcase

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Maybe this means we won't need to use as much of their Compassare.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Fatutu ... Fatutu?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Emm?
The room where they were making Sea Mother's Eyes together is empty now.
All the Sea Mother's Eyes have been completed, neatly lined up against the wall.
The palm-bark shells are finely woven, carefully crafted, decorated with white seashells, and seamlessly merged with the Compassare roots.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: She finished them already! Did she even sleep?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Where did she go?
She rushes out from the room like a stirring wind.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Miss Barcarola?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I ... I can't find Fatutu.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Miss Fatutu?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: We promised to make the Sea Mother's Eyes together, but she finished all of them during the night! And now she's gone.
Sonetto frowns, thinking.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Today's the Suitcase Trade Fair. There'll be more people around than usual. Let's split up and ask around. See if anyone's seen her.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Great!
Her skirt flutters behind her as she dashes off in search of her friend.
Camp - Morning
An open-air campsite is starting to take shape into the impromptu Suitcase Trade Fair.
Half-open crates, rolled-up clothes, signs, standing lamps, little tents.
Barcarola weaves through the scattered clutter as Fatutu's name lies coiled on her tongue.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: So long as Fatutu can hear me, she won't just stay quiet.
She inhales deeply, building up a voice that could rival any instrument, just about to shout—
—when a hand taps her on the shoulder.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Miss Barcarola.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Huff—*cough*
The gasp of air chokes her all at once, and she's left coughing uncontrollably.
The culprit gently pats her, waiting for the coughing to settle.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We've found Fatutu.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Is she alright? Is she safe?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I think she needs a bit of time to herself. Sonetto and I chose not to disturb her.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She'll reach out again when the time is right.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Would you be willing to be there when that moment comes?
Barcarola's feet answer faster than her mouth.
She leaves behind only the sight of her retreating back and a voice drifting from afar.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Of course, I would!
